editorial:
Imagine you are stuck in 1950s Mexico City, feeling totally alone and out of place. That is exactly where you find William, an American guy who spends his days hiding from the world. Everything changes when he meets Eugene, a younger student who is just as messy and lost as he is. The vibe here is very moody and slow, making you feel the heat of the city and the desperation of two people trying to find some kind of love or comfort in a world that does not really want them. It is a story about longing and the strange ways people try to connect when they feel broken.

Daniel Craig does an amazing job playing a man who is falling apart at the seams. You will love how the colors and lighting make the city feel alive, though the slow pace might be a bit much if you are looking for a fast story. If you enjoy deep character studies, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: By the end, the relationship between William and Eugene falls apart because it was built on a shaky foundation of need and drugs. William realizes that he cannot force someone to love him or save him from his own sadness. He ends up alone again, but he has a better understanding of himself. The movie wraps up with a feeling of quiet sadness, showing that some connections are just temporary lessons in life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional dramas and great acting.
